name: New Rules and Clarifications: Blood & Willpower

pages.name: New Rules and Clarifications: Blood & Willpower

text.content:
A short appendix of general, system-wide rules clarifications and additions covering Blood and Willpower. These are not elder-specific; they apply to any Kindred character.

Blood Addiction

Lupine blood is addictive to Kindred. Whenever a Kindred feeds from a Lupine, he must undertake a Static Mental Challenge, with difficulty equal to the sum of the Lupine's current Rage and Gnosis Traits. If the Kindred wins, he is free of addiction. If he loses, he gains the Derangement Addicted and must feed on Lupine blood whenever possible; failing to do so on a regular basis may provoke frenzy, sending the Kindred after the nearest Lupine.

An addicted Kindred may attempt to "kick the habit" by spending a Willpower Trait and retesting the original Static Challenge. This retest may be attempted only once; failure means the character automatically frenzies on the Derangement.

Blood Expenditures

Normal blood expenditure limits apply in all cases except where a Discipline would otherwise require a vampire to spend more blood in a turn than his generation allows. In such cases, the Kindred may spend blood in excess of his generation's normal per-turn limit, but only to activate that specific Discipline.

Example: a vampire with Form of the Beast may spend the three Blood Traits the power requires to change to the desired form instantly, even if that exceeds what his generation would otherwise allow him to spend in a single turn — but he may not spend additional blood for any other purpose until the next turn.

Blood Storage

To store mortal blood successfully (rather than ending up with a refrigerator of clotted gunk), a character needs a Medical Ability rating of at least two, or at least one level of the Health Influence. Properly stored human blood keeps for one month; after that, even under the best conditions, it goes bad. Drinking bad blood provides no nourishment, and may cause the vampire to vomit up good blood already in his system.

Kindred vitae behaves very differently from mortal blood. Carefully stored, it can provide nourishment, pleasure, or serve for a blood bond for a much longer time: a neonate's blood rarely lasts more than a year, while a Methuselah's blood may retain its potency for a century or longer.

Note: questions of blood potency also apply to drinks left for Kindred resting in torpor.

Blood Traits of Food Sources

The number of Blood Traits available from various creatures, and what happens to a source drained completely:

Food SourceBlood Traits
Cat1
Chicken1
Rat1
Child2
Dog2
Human4
Cow8
Garou8

A food source that is drained completely dies. Humans and animals lose two Health Levels per Blood Trait taken, and die if completely drained. Garou are hardier: they lose one Health Level for every two Blood Traits taken.

Willpower

Replenishing Willpower

Willpower is replenished in full once the Storyteller determines the story is over. The process of replenishment takes exactly as long as the Storyteller says it does.

Staying Awake

A vampire must spend one Willpower Trait for every four hours after sunrise during which he wishes to remain awake and active. This applies regardless of whether the vampire is moving about in daylight or simply staying conscious in the darkest, deepest crypt — the sun being in the sky overhead is what matters, not exposure to it. Given this cost, a vampire cannot stay awake through an entire day very often.

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference.JournalEntry.7f69a74f36db4a08]{Frenzy}

A Willpower Trait may be spent to stave off frenzy for 10 minutes. If the character has not removed herself from whatever is provoking her by the end of that time, she must spend another Willpower Trait to hold off frenzy for another 10 minutes. This continues until the character either escapes the provocation, runs out of Willpower, or gives in and frenzies.

Replenishing Traits

Once per night, a character may spend a Willpower Trait to regain all lost Traits in one Attribute category (Social, Physical, or Mental). A single Willpower Trait only restores one category — restoring all three categories in the same night requires spending a separate Willpower Trait for each one. This expenditure is limited to once per category per night.

Ignoring Wounds

A character without the Endurance benefit against wound penalties may spend one Willpower Trait to ignore all wound penalties for a single challenge. Characters with Celerity should note that each additional action is a separate challenge, requiring a new Willpower Trait for every action in which the character wants to ignore his wound penalties.
